newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Richter says H1 op margin up on strong dlr.
newsitem.headline: Richter says H1 op margin up on strong dlr.

text.p: Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Richter Gedeon Vegyeszeti Gyar Rt's operating margins rose in the first half of the year on the back of the dollar's strength, the company said in its earnings report.
"Operating margins were 31.2 percent in the first half of 1997 compared with 28.9 percent for the same period in 1996," Richter said on Thursday.
"Margins benefited from the continuing strength of the U.S. dollar, primarily as the majority of exports are invoiced in U.S. dollars," it added.
The company added that while most exports were invoiced in U.S. dollars, operating expenses incurred primarily in Hungarian forints.

Richter released its first half IAS earnings report on Thursday and reported its net profit rising to 9.507 billion forints on sales of 24.837 billion from a net profit of 6.527 billion on sales of 18.070 billion in the first half of 1996.
Within total revenues, the company's sales in Hungary rose to 7.512 billion forints from 6.071 billion.

"In the domestic market, Hungary, pressure on Government health expenditure budget continues to impact volumes generally," Richter said. "Notwithstanding this, first half 1997 sales increased 23.7 percent to 7.512 billion forints."

Richter's exports amounted to $98 million for the January-June period, an increase of $14.6 million or 17.5 percent over the same six months of 1996 attributed primarily to strong demand from the CIS countries.
